title: Ergonomic Chairs
blurb: Lumbar support, adjustability, and picks for tighter budgets.
lede: A good chair should adjust to you, not the other way around: seat depth, lumbar support, and armrest height all matter more than the brand name.

products.name: Herman Miller Aeron
products.desc: Breathable Pellicle mesh over a die-cast frame, with adjustable PostureFit lumbar support.

products.name: Steelcase Series 1
products.desc: A knit-mesh back and a simpler lumbar mechanism, most of the adjustability at a gentler price.

products.name: Branch Ergonomic Chair
products.desc: Mesh back with a fixed lumbar pad — a sensible starting point under real budget constraints.

title: Standing Desks
blurb: Sit-stand desks and converters that actually stay stable.
lede: Alternating between sitting and standing through the day is one of the cheapest ways to reduce stiffness. Look for a stable frame and a quiet motor.

products.name: Uplift V2 Standing Desk
products.desc: A dual-motor frame that stays rock-solid at full height, with a memory keypad for quick position changes.

products.name: FlexiSpot E7 Pro
products.desc: Dual motors and strong weight capacity for less than most premium competitors.

products.name: Standing Desk Converter
products.desc: Sits on your existing desk and lifts keyboard and monitor together — no installation required.

title: Monitor Arms & Mounts
blurb: Get your screen to eye level and free up desk space.
lede: Your monitor's top edge should sit near eye level, roughly an arm's length away. A good arm makes that adjustment a five-second task instead of a permanent compromise.

products.name: Ergotron LX Monitor Arm
products.desc: A gas-spring arm with smooth, well-damped movement across a wide height range.

products.name: VIVO Dual Monitor Desk Mount
products.desc: Independent height and tilt for two screens side by side, clamped straight to the desk.

products.name: Laptop Stand + External Keyboard
products.desc: An aluminum riser plus a separate keyboard — the single highest-impact fix for laptop-only setups.

title: Keyboards & Mice
blurb: Split and low-profile options that go easier on your wrists.
lede: Wrist strain usually comes from a flat keyboard angle plus reaching too far for the mouse. Split or low-profile boards, plus a mouse that fits your hand, both help.

products.name: Logitech Ergo K860
products.desc: A gently curved, split layout with a built-in palm rest for a more neutral wrist angle.

products.name: Logitech MX Keys
products.desc: Low-profile, quiet keys and reliable switching across several paired devices.

products.name: Logitech MX Master 3S
products.desc: A shape that supports the whole hand rather than just the fingertips over an eight-hour day.

title: Desk Lighting
blurb: Reduce eye strain during long video-call days.
lede: Good lighting is an eye-strain fix as much as a comfort one — especially on video calls where you're staring at a screen for hours.

products.name: BenQ ScreenBar
products.desc: Clips onto the monitor and lights the desk without glaring back at the screen.

products.name: Adjustable LED Desk Lamp
products.desc: Adjustable color temperature and brightness to match the light to the time of day.

products.name: Compact Key Light
products.desc: A small, diffused light aimed at your face — a bigger difference on camera than most webcam upgrades.

title: Accessories
blurb: Cable management, footrests, and anti-fatigue mats.
lede: Smaller upgrades that round out a setup once the big pieces — chair, desk, monitor height — are already sorted.

products.name: Anti-Fatigue Mat
products.desc: A cushioned, non-slip mat that makes standing sessions noticeably more comfortable.

products.name: Ergonomic Footrest
products.desc: A tilting, textured rest for desks that leave your feet without solid ground.

products.name: Under-Desk Cable Tray
products.desc: A clamp-on tray that keeps cables clear of a sit-stand desk's moving legs — no drilling.
